verdict.rationale: ESD's own guidance names a sanctioned third-party channel: 'firms that represent employers' can manage tasks in eServices, and EAMS supports adding an employer, which suggests a representative firm can act for multiple employer accounts. How a firm is designated or authorized, what it may do, and how the employer grants or revokes that authority are not documented in the open pages. The transactional portal sits behind a login and was not examined. Missing for 10: documented designation/authorization process (e.g., power-of-attorney or third-party administrator forms), scope of delegated permissions, revocation controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, the service documents a sanctioned third-party rail — designees, authorized providers, registered agents, or representatives — through which a provider can act for my company

citations.quote: Employers and firms that represent employers can manage many tasks in eServices.
Watch this 2-minute video to learn how to add an employer in EAMS.
